BatchGetTraces.name: BatchGetTraces
BatchGetTraces.doc: You cannot find traces through this API if Transaction Search is enabled since trace is not indexed in X-Ray. Retrieves a list of traces specified by ID. Each trace is a collection of segment documents that originates from a single request. Use GetTraceSummaries to get a list of trace IDs.

CancelTraceRetrieval.name: CancelTraceRetrieval
CancelTraceRetrieval.doc: Cancels an ongoing trace retrieval job initiated by StartTraceRetrieval using the provided RetrievalToken. A successful cancellation will return an HTTP 200 response.

CreateGroup.name: CreateGroup
CreateGroup.doc: Creates a group resource with a name and a filter expression.

CreateSamplingRule.name: CreateSamplingRule
CreateSamplingRule.doc: Creates a rule to control sampling behavior for instrumented applications. Services retrieve rules with GetSamplingRules, and evaluate each rule in ascending order of priority for each request. If a rule matches, the service records a trace, borrowing it from the reservoir size. After 10 seconds, the service reports back to X-Ray with GetSamplingTargets to get updated versions of each in-use…

DeleteResourcePolicy.name: DeleteResourcePolicy
DeleteResourcePolicy.doc: Deletes a resource policy from the target Amazon Web Services account.

GetEncryptionConfig.name: GetEncryptionConfig
GetEncryptionConfig.doc: Retrieves the current encryption configuration for X-Ray data.

GetIndexingRules.name: GetIndexingRules
GetIndexingRules.doc: Retrieves all indexing rules. Indexing rules are used to determine the server-side sampling rate for spans ingested through the CloudWatchLogs destination and indexed by X-Ray. For more information, see Transaction Search.

GetInsight.name: GetInsight
GetInsight.doc: Retrieves the summary information of an insight. This includes impact to clients and root cause services, the top anomalous services, the category, the state of the insight, and the start and end time of the insight.

GetInsightEvents.name: GetInsightEvents
GetInsightEvents.doc: X-Ray reevaluates insights periodically until they're resolved, and records each intermediate state as an event. You can review an insight's events in the Impact Timeline on the Inspect page in the X-Ray console.

GetInsightImpactGraph.name: GetInsightImpactGraph
GetInsightImpactGraph.doc: Retrieves a service graph structure filtered by the specified insight. The service graph is limited to only structural information. For a complete service graph, use this API with the GetServiceGraph API.

GetInsightSummaries.name: GetInsightSummaries
GetInsightSummaries.doc: Retrieves the summaries of all insights in the specified group matching the provided filter values.

GetRetrievedTracesGraph.name: GetRetrievedTracesGraph
GetRetrievedTracesGraph.doc: Retrieves a service graph for traces based on the specified RetrievalToken from the CloudWatch log group generated by Transaction Search. This API does not initiate a retrieval job. You must first execute StartTraceRetrieval to obtain the required RetrievalToken. The trace graph describes services that process incoming requests and any downstream services they call, which may include Amazon Web…

GetSamplingStatisticSummaries.name: GetSamplingStatisticSummaries
GetSamplingStatisticSummaries.doc: Retrieves information about recent sampling results for all sampling rules.

GetSamplingTargets.name: GetSamplingTargets
GetSamplingTargets.doc: Requests a sampling quota for rules that the service is using to sample requests.

GetServiceGraph.name: GetServiceGraph
GetServiceGraph.doc: Retrieves a document that describes services that process incoming requests, and downstream services that they call as a result. Root services process incoming requests and make calls to downstream services. Root services are applications that use the Amazon Web Services X-Ray SDK. Downstream services can be other applications, Amazon Web Services resources, HTTP web APIs, or SQL databases.

GetTimeSeriesServiceStatistics.name: GetTimeSeriesServiceStatistics
GetTimeSeriesServiceStatistics.doc: Get an aggregation of service statistics defined by a specific time range.

GetTraceGraph.name: GetTraceGraph
GetTraceGraph.doc: Retrieves a service graph for one or more specific trace IDs.

GetTraceSegmentDestination.name: GetTraceSegmentDestination
GetTraceSegmentDestination.doc: Retrieves the current destination of data sent to PutTraceSegments and OpenTelemetry protocol (OTLP) endpoint. The Transaction Search feature requires a CloudWatchLogs destination. For more information, see Transaction Search and OpenTelemetry.

GetTraceSummaries.name: GetTraceSummaries
GetTraceSummaries.doc: Retrieves IDs and annotations for traces available for a specified time frame using an optional filter. To get the full traces, pass the trace IDs to BatchGetTraces. A filter expression can target traced requests that hit specific service nodes or edges, have errors, or come from a known user. ListResourcePolicies.name: ListResourcePolicies
ListResourcePolicies.doc: Returns the list of resource policies in the target Amazon Web Services account.

ListRetrievedTraces.name: ListRetrievedTraces
ListRetrievedTraces.doc: Retrieves a list of traces for a given RetrievalToken from the CloudWatch log group generated by Transaction Search. For information on what each trace returns, see BatchGetTraces. This API does not initiate a retrieval process. To start a trace retrieval, use StartTraceRetrieval, which generates the required RetrievalToken. When the RetrievalStatus is not COMPLETE, the API will return an empty…

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.doc: Returns a list of tags that are applied to the specified Amazon Web Services X-Ray group or sampling rule.

PutEncryptionConfig.name: PutEncryptionConfig
PutEncryptionConfig.doc: Updates the encryption configuration for X-Ray data.

PutResourcePolicy.name: PutResourcePolicy
PutResourcePolicy.doc: Sets the resource policy to grant one or more Amazon Web Services services and accounts permissions to access X-Ray. Each resource policy will be associated with a specific Amazon Web Services account. Each Amazon Web Services account can have a maximum of 5 resource policies, and each policy name must be unique within that account. The maximum size of each resource policy is 5KB.

PutTelemetryRecords.name: PutTelemetryRecords
PutTelemetryRecords.doc: Used by the Amazon Web Services X-Ray daemon to upload telemetry.

PutTraceSegments.name: PutTraceSegments
PutTraceSegments.doc: Uploads segment documents to Amazon Web Services X-Ray. A segment document can be a completed segment, an in-progress segment, or an array of subsegments. Segments must include the following fields. For the full segment document schema, see Amazon Web Services X-Ray Segment Documents in the Amazon Web Services X-Ray Developer Guide. Required segment document fields name - The name of the service…

StartTraceRetrieval.name: StartTraceRetrieval
StartTraceRetrieval.doc: Initiates a trace retrieval process using the specified time range and for the given trace IDs in the Transaction Search generated CloudWatch log group. For more information, see Transaction Search. API returns a RetrievalToken, which can be used with ListRetrievedTraces or GetRetrievedTracesGraph to fetch results. Retrievals will time out after 60 minutes. To execute long time ranges, consider…

TagResource.name: TagResource
TagResource.doc: Applies tags to an existing Amazon Web Services X-Ray group or sampling rule.

UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.doc: Removes tags from an Amazon Web Services X-Ray group or sampling rule. You cannot edit or delete system tags (those with an aws: prefix).

UpdateIndexingRule.name: UpdateIndexingRule
UpdateIndexingRule.doc: Modifies an indexing rule’s configuration. Indexing rules are used for determining the sampling rate for spans indexed from CloudWatch Logs. For more information, see Transaction Search.

UpdateTraceSegmentDestination.name: UpdateTraceSegmentDestination
UpdateTraceSegmentDestination.doc: Modifies the destination of data sent to PutTraceSegments. The Transaction Search feature requires the CloudWatchLogs destination. For more information, see Transaction Search.

Duration.doc: The length of time in seconds between the start time of the root span and the end time of the last span that completed.

RetrievedTrace.doc: Retrieved collection of spans with matching trace IDs.

RootCauseException.doc: The exception associated with a root cause.

MaxRate.doc: Defines max temporary sampling rate to apply when a boost is triggered. Calculated boost rate by X-Ray will be less than or equal to this max rate.

CooldownWindowMinutes.doc: Sets the time window (in minutes) in which only one sampling rate boost can be triggered. After a boost occurs, no further boosts are allowed until the next window.

SamplingRateBoost.doc: Enable temporary sampling rate increases when you detect anomalies to improve visibility.

ModifiedAt.doc: When the rule was last modified.

ReservoirQuota.doc: The number of requests per second that X-Ray allocated for this service.

Interval.doc: The number of seconds for the service to wait before getting sampling targets again.

SamplingBoost.doc: The sampling boost that X-Ray allocated for this service.

SamplingTargetDocument.doc: Temporary changes to a sampling rule configuration. To meet the global sampling target for a rule, X-Ray calculates a new reservoir for each service based on the recent sampling results of all services that called GetSamplingTargets.

Segment.doc: A segment from a trace that has been ingested by the X-Ray service. The segment can be compiled from documents uploaded with PutTraceSegments, or an inferred segment for a downstream service, generated from a subsegment sent by the service that called it. For the full segment document schema, see Amazon Web Services X-Ray segment documents in the Amazon Web Services X-Ray Developer Guide.

ReferenceId.doc: Identifier for the service. Unique within the service map.

Name.doc: The canonical name of the service.

Names.doc: A list of names for the service, including the canonical name.

Root.doc: Indicates that the service was the first service to process a request.

AccountId.doc: Identifier of the Amazon Web Services account in which the service runs.

Type.doc: The type of service. Amazon Web Services Resource - The type of an Amazon Web Services resource. For example, AWS::EC2::Instance for an application running on Amazon EC2 or AWS::DynamoDB::Table for an Amazon DynamoDB table that the application used. StartTime.doc: The start time of the first segment that the service generated.

EndTime.doc: The end time of the last segment that the service generated.

DurationHistogram.doc: A histogram that maps the spread of service durations.

ResponseTimeHistogram.doc: A histogram that maps the spread of service response times.

Service.doc: Information about an application that processed requests, users that made requests, or downstream services, resources, and applications that an application used.

OkCount.doc: The number of requests that completed with a 2xx Success status code.

ErrorStatistics.doc: Information about requests that failed with a 4xx Client Error status code.

FaultStatistics.doc: Information about requests that failed with a 5xx Server Error status code.

TotalCount.doc: The total number of completed requests.

TotalResponseTime.doc: The aggregate response time of completed requests.

Span.doc: A span from a trace that has been ingested by the X-Ray service. A span represents a unit of work or an operation performed by a service.

TraceIds.doc: Specify the trace IDs of the traces to be retrieved.

StartTime.doc: The start of the time range to retrieve traces. The range is inclusive, so the specified start time is included in the query. Specified as epoch time, the number of seconds since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC.

EndTime.doc: The end of the time range to retrieve traces. The range is inclusive, so the specified end time is included in the query. Specified as epoch time, the number of seconds since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC.

Key.doc: A tag key, such as Stage or Name. A tag key cannot be empty. The key can be a maximum of 128 characters, and can contain only Unicode letters, numbers, or separators, or the following special characters: + - = . _ : /

Value.doc: An optional tag value, such as Production or test-only. The value can be a maximum of 255 characters, and contain only Unicode letters, numbers, or separators, or the following special characters: + - = . _ : /

Tag.doc: A map that contains tag keys and tag values to attach to an Amazon Web Services X-Ray group or sampling rule. For more information about ways to use tags, see Tagging Amazon Web Services resources in the Amazon Web Services General Reference. ResourceARN.doc: The Amazon Resource Number (ARN) of an X-Ray group or sampling rule.

Tags.doc: A map that contains one or more tag keys and tag values to attach to an X-Ray group or sampling rule. For more information about ways to use tags, see Tagging Amazon Web Services resources in the Amazon Web Services General Reference. The following restrictions apply to tags: Maximum number of user-applied tags per resource: 50 Maximum tag key length: 128 Unicode characters Maximum tag value…

Timestamp.doc: Timestamp of the window for which statistics are aggregated.

ServiceForecastStatistics.doc: The forecasted high and low fault count values.

ResponseTimeHistogram.doc: The response time histogram for the selected entities.

Duration.doc: The length of time in seconds between the start time of the earliest segment that started and the end time of the last segment that completed.

LimitExceeded.doc: LimitExceeded is set to true when the trace has exceeded the Trace document size limit. For more information about this limit and other X-Ray limits and quotas, see Amazon Web Services X-Ray endpoints and quotas.

Segments.doc: Segment documents for the segments and subsegments that comprise the trace.

Trace.doc: A collection of segment documents with matching trace IDs.

Id.doc: The unique identifier for the request that generated the trace's segments and subsegments.

StartTime.doc: The start time of a trace, based on the earliest trace segment start time.

Duration.doc: The length of time in seconds between the start time of the earliest segment that started and the end time of the last segment that completed.

ResponseTime.doc: The length of time in seconds between the start and end times of the root segment. If the service performs work asynchronously, the response time measures the time before the response is sent to the user, while the duration measures the amount of time before the last traced activity completes.

HasFault.doc: The root segment document has a 500 series error.

HasError.doc: The root segment document has a 400 series error.

HasThrottle.doc: One or more of the segment documents has a 429 throttling error.

IsPartial.doc: One or more of the segment documents is in progress.

Http.doc: Information about the HTTP request served by the trace.

Annotations.doc: Annotations from the trace's segment documents.

Users.doc: Users from the trace's segment documents.

ServiceIds.doc: Service IDs from the trace's segment documents.

ResourceARNs.doc: A list of resource ARNs for any resource corresponding to the trace segments.

InstanceIds.doc: A list of EC2 instance IDs for any instance corresponding to the trace segments.

AvailabilityZones.doc: A list of Availability Zones for any zone corresponding to the trace segments.

FaultRootCauses.doc: A collection of FaultRootCause structures corresponding to the trace segments.

ErrorRootCauses.doc: A collection of ErrorRootCause structures corresponding to the trace segments.

ResponseTimeRootCauses.doc: A collection of ResponseTimeRootCause structures corresponding to the trace segments.

Revision.doc: The revision number of a trace.

MatchedEventTime.doc: The matched time stamp of a defined event.

TraceSummary.doc: Metadata generated from the segment documents in a trace.

ServiceIds.doc: Services that the user's request hit.

TraceUser.doc: Information about a user recorded in segment documents.

RuleName.doc: The name of the sampling rule.

UnprocessedStatistics.doc: Sampling statistics from a call to GetSamplingTargets that X-Ray could not process.

ErrorCode.doc: The error that caused processing to fail.

UnprocessedTraceSegment.doc: Information about a segment that failed processing.

ResourceARN.doc: The Amazon Resource Number (ARN) of an X-Ray group or sampling rule.

TagKeys.doc: Keys for one or more tags that you want to remove from an X-Ray group or sampling rule.

GroupName.doc: The case-sensitive name of the group.

GroupARN.doc: The ARN that was generated upon creation.

FilterExpression.doc: The updated filter expression defining criteria by which to group traces.

InsightsConfiguration.doc: The structure containing configurations related to insights. The InsightsEnabled boolean can be set to true to enable insights for the group or false to disable insights for the group. The NotificationsEnabled boolean can be set to true to enable insights notifications for the group. Notifications can only be enabled on a group with InsightsEnabled set to true.

Group.doc: The group that was updated. Contains the name of the group that was updated, the ARN of the group that was updated, the updated filter expression, and the updated insight configuration assigned to the group.

Name.doc: Name of the indexing rule to be updated.

SamplingRuleUpdate.doc: The rule and fields to change.

SamplingRuleRecord.doc: The updated rule definition and metadata.

Destination.doc: The configured destination of trace segments.
The destination of the trace segments.
